terms.definition: A stretching of Earth's oceans caused by the Moon's (and Sun's) gravity; two bulges exist at all times, one near-side and one far-side.
The difference in gravitational pull across Earth's width, which is what actually creates both tidal bulges, including the far-side one.
Extra-high and extra-low tides that happen when the Sun and Moon are aligned (New or Full Moon), combining their pulls.
Milder tides that happen when the Sun and Moon are at right angles (quarter moons), partly cancelling each other's pull.
